summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would adjust fuel tax credit calculations and related rules to support the reintroduction of fuel duty indexation through separate customs and excise bills.
Credits would generally use the duty rate applying when fuel was acquired or imported, or when locally manufactured fuel entered home consumption.
The fuel credit amendments would commence on 31 July 2014 and apply to tax periods starting, and relevant returns lodged, from 1 July 2014.
changes: The separate duty-rate rule for unregistered fuel credit claimants would be removed.
The road user charge would be rounded from 26.14 cents to 26.1 cents from 1 August 2014.
Future road user charges would also be rounded to one decimal place of a cent.
Fuel would not attract blend duties solely because indexation caused different duty rates on its components.
Cleaner fuel rebates would use the biodiesel rate applying when the fuel entered home consumption.
summary.affected: Fuel tax credit claimants, heavy vehicle operators and cleaner fuel producers would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Christopher Pyne
speeches.brief: Moved a debate management motion limiting consideration of the four fuel indexation bills to a set process, including capping the detail stage at 30 minutes, to ensure the government's fuel excise legislation passes that day.
